issues.failure_explanation: For L = I⊗A + A⊗I the eigenvalues are λ_i+λ_j, so σ_min(L) is generally not 2σ_min(A). It already fails for normal matrices: A=[[-ε,1],[-1,-ε]] has σ_min(A)=sqrt(1+ε²) but L has the eigenvalue -2ε, so σ_min(L)≤2ε. The same identity is reused for ||L^{-1}||_2 in the bound on ||L^{-1}Π||_2. The resulting residual-to-error bound and the constant γ are therefore not valid upper bounds for general (non-symmetric) Hurwitz A.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace 2σ_min(A) by a valid lower bound on σ_min(L). One option is 2λ_min(-(A+A^T)/2), valid under dissipativity. Otherwise compute or bound σ_min(L) directly. Restate Prop. 1, Thm. 1 and the scaling accordingly, possibly restricting the class of A.
issues.overall_effect: The 'rigorous, computable' certificate (Prop. 1, Thm. 1, the stopping criterion, the O(n) estimate of sigma_min and the scaling (eq:52)) is unreliable for general Hurwitz A. The numerical validation of the certificate is also affected.
issues.title: False identity sigma_min(L)=2 sigma_min(A) invalidates the error-residual bound
issues.why_classification: A contained replacement lemma restores the bound, but the general-Hurwitz scope and the O(n) computability of the constant are lost or must be re-argued.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: $\fX_k = \fZ_k\fZ_k^\T$ is the unique solution of the Lyapunov equation~\eqref{alg:statIterGLE:lyap} in iteration $k$ of \Cref{alg:statIterGLE}

issues.failure_explanation: Prop. 2 is derived for the exact stationary iteration, in which B_k is built from the exact X_{k-1}. In Algorithm 1 with inexact solves, B_k is built from the approximate Z_{k-1}. The 'exact' X_k and X_{k-1} of the proof therefore do not satisfy the error recursion (eq31). The inequality ||X-X_k|| ≤ γ||X_k-X_{k-1}||_F is used without justification. The correct comparison is between X_k and the approximate X̃_{k-1}.

failure_location.quote: Let $\fX_k$ be the exact solution of the Lyapunov equation~\eqref{alg:statIterGLE:lyap} computed at step $k$ of \Cref{alg:statIterGLE}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Redo the recursion with the perturbed right-hand side to get ||X-X_k|| ≤ γ||X_k-X̃_{k-1}||. Then bound ||X_k-X̃_{k-1}|| by R_k/(2σ_min)+Δ. This gives (eq:50) or a slightly sharper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The proof of the stated bound (eq:50) is not valid as written, although a corrected derivation likely gives a bound of the same form.
issues.title: Theorem 1 applies Prop. 2 to an inexact iteration outside its hypotheses
issues.why_classification: The repair is a short local re-derivation that keeps the result and its form.

issues.failure_explanation: From A+A^T≺0 one only gets -w^T A w ≥ λ_min(-(A+A^T)/2)||w||², and this quantity is at most σ_min(A). The proof needs -w^T A w ≥ σ_n(A)||w||², which fails in general. Counterexample: the normal matrix A=[[-ε,1],[-1,-ε]] has σ_n(A)=sqrt(1+ε²) but -w^T A w=ε||w||². The chosen μ=κ(A_j)·tol can then be too small, so the claim that X̂ satisfies the LMI is not established and is false in general.

failure_location.quote: where we used the fact that $\fw^{\T}\fA_j^{\T}\fw<0$ for all

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace κ(A_j) by σ_1(A_j)/λ_min(-(A_j+A_j^T)/2) in (eqn:ass:teo4) and (eqn:cond:LMI). The same short proof then works, and the experiments are recomputed.
issues.overall_effect: The perturbation constant (eqn:cond:LMI) and Table 1 are not justified in general. The discussion of normal/port-Hamiltonian matrices is not covered by the proof.
issues.title: Theorem 4 proof uses a false lower bound w^T A^T w ≤ -σ_n(A)||w||²
issues.why_classification: The fix is short but changes the theorem's constant, which may become much larger. The quantitative claims and the sharpness discussion are affected.

issues.failure_explanation: Stability preservation in square-root balanced truncation needs the Lyapunov inequalities for the Gramians used. It also needs a nonempty retained block whose singular values are disjoint from the truncated ones (or an equivalent condition), together with positivity/minimality. The proposition assumes none of this. The proof only appeals to 'generalized Gramian' interpretation. Equal singular values across the truncation cut, which the paper itself discusses, can yield non-asymptotically-stable reduced matrices.

failure_location.quote: Therefore, each $\tilde \fA_j$ is, by construction, stable due to the stability properties of classical square root balance truncation.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the hypothesis Σ_1 and Σ_2 have disjoint spectra with Σ_1≻0. Verify the mode-j Lyapunov inequalities, and note that the guarantee holds only for exact solves.
issues.overall_effect: The claimed advantage of PBR (stable subsystems guaranteed) is unsupported for arbitrary r. Approximate Gramians are not covered either, since the proposition assumes exact solves.
issues.title: Per-mode stability of PBR ROMs claimed without the separation hypothesis
issues.why_classification: Adding a standard classical condition repairs the statement without changing the method.

issues.failure_explanation: The statement defines H_o using λ_1(M_c(·)), but the proof produces the term λ_1(M_o(·))∫||X_o||². M_c and M_o have different spectra, so the stated bound (eq:err:est:2) does not follow from the proof. M_o is also defined with Σ_jĀ_j^T and C̄C̄^T instead of the Lyapunov form used in the proof, and the proof inequality is written with ||X||.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Define H_o with λ_1(M_o), where M_o = Ā^TΣ+ΣĀ+C̄^TC̄. Correct the transposes in the M_c/M_o definitions and propagate to Thm. 6.
issues.overall_effect: The inequality as stated is not what is proved. The definitions entering Thm. 6 and the experimental quantities χ must be corrected.
issues.title: Lemma 5: H_o defined with λ_1(M_c) although the proof yields λ_1(M_o); M_o,M_c definitions inconsistent
issues.why_classification: The correct definitions are visible from the proof, and the repair is a local relabelling.

issues.failure_explanation: Lemma 5 gives error² ≤ H − G + 4σ²||u||². Taking square roots, the G-contribution is sqrt(−G) with a plus sign, active when G<0. The theorem instead writes −G^{1/2} H(−G). On the support of H(−G) we have G<0, so G^{1/2} is non-real. The leading minus sign would also lower the bound exactly where the LMI violation should increase it.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the term by +Σ (−G)^{1/2} H(−G), and likewise in ι.
issues.overall_effect: The stated bound (eq:err:est:3), and the experimental quantity ι (eqn:iota) copied from it, is ill-defined as a real bound and has the wrong sign.
issues.title: Theorem 6: G-term has wrong sign and takes square root of a negative quantity
issues.why_classification: The correction is forced by Lemma 5 and is a single-term fix.

issues.failure_explanation: The classical telescoping argument truncates one block of Hankel singular values at a time through a chain of intermediate reduced models. Here each mode has its own balanced coordinates and different projectors V_j, W_j. The jump maps W_{q_k}^T V_{q_{k-1}} and the Lemma 5 hypotheses are not shown to be compatible across the intermediate orders s_k, s_{k+1} and across all modes. No argument is given for the intermediate systems or the jump terms G, and the claim that the multiplicities m_k(j) are equal across modes is only assumed. The step is nontrivial and missing.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the iteration argument: define the nested intermediate PBR models, verify that Lemma 5 applies to each consecutive pair with the transition maps, and sum with sub-additivity.

issues.failure_explanation: A_1 = -I + (1/2)S with S the shift is not normal, since SS^T≠S^TS. A_2 is tridiagonal Toeplitz with sub/super entries 4/5 and -1/5, and A_2A_2^T-A_2^TA_2=(a²-b²)(SS^T-S^TS)≠0. The stated justification for Thm. 4's hypothesis therefore fails. A_j+A_j^T≺0 does hold, so the hypothesis is true but for an unstated reason. The reported κ(A_j) values and the 'normal' framing are also unsupported.

failure_location.quote: Moreover, both $\fA_1$ and $\fA_2$ are normal matrices, so the hypothesis of \Cref{teo4} holds.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Verify (eqn:ass:ndeAj) directly, e.g. by noting the eigenvalues of A_j+A_j^T are negative, and drop the normality claim.
issues.overall_effect: Only the justification for applying Thm. 4 in the example is wrong; the dissipativity itself holds.
